author: Keystone Today
title: Jamaican national sentenced to 54 months for role in lottery scam targeting elderly
text:
Tajay Singh, a resident of Montego Bay, Jamaica, was sentenced on May 13 to 54 months in federal prison for his involvement in an international lottery scam that targeted elderly victims. United States District Judge Robert J. Colville imposed the sentence following Singh’s conviction for wire fraud and money laundering.
The case highlights ongoing concerns about scams that prey on older adults by promising large winnings in exchange for upfront payments. Prosecutors say such schemes can cause significant financial harm and emotional distress to vulnerable populations.
According to information presented to the court, from January 2021 through October 2023, Singh conspired with others to defraud elderly individuals by telling them they had won a lottery but needed to pay taxes and fees before collecting their prize. After victims sent money as instructed, they never received any winnings. The scheme involved using other conspirators and victims, bank accounts opened in victims’ names, wire transfers, purchases of physical goods, and ATM withdrawals in Jamaica as part of efforts to carry out and conceal the fraud.
Assistant United States Attorney Kelly M. Locher prosecuted the case on behalf of the government. United States Attorney Troy Rivetti said the investigation leading up to Singh’s prosecution was conducted by the Federal Bureau of Investigation, Homeland Security Investigations, and the United States Postal Inspection Service.
The sentencing underscores law enforcement efforts against transnational fraud schemes targeting seniors.
